The test image shows a corn ear with dark green to blue-green mold extensively covering kernels. This is a seed/ear disease.

Top candidates from the seed/pod part index: Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Gibberella_Disease, Diplodia_Ear_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Trichoderma reference shows dark blue-green mold on yellow kernels, very similar pattern to test image. Let me check other candidates.
Aspergillus is olive-green/yellowish powdery mold, clearly different from the dark blue-green in the test image. Now checking other ear rot candidates.
Fusarium shows whitish-pink mold, not matching. Let me continue checking other classes.
Gibberella shows red/pink mold at ear tip, not matching. Let me check more classes.
Diplodia shows white/grayish-brown mold, not matching. Let me check more distinct classes.
Common Smut shows large silvery-white galls, completely different. Let me check Head_Smut and Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight on ear.
Head Smut shows dark spore masses replacing the ear, completely different. Now let me view a second Trichoderma reference to confirm the match.

This shows the dark green Trichoderma conidia on husk leaves, consistent with the disease. The test image matches Trichoderma_Ear_Rot very well:

- **Dark blue-green mold** covering kernels extensively (matches "dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels")
- Mold is on and between the kernels across the ear
- Yellow kernels visible beneath the dark green fungal growth
- The color is distinctly dark blue-green, not olive-green (ruling out Aspergillus), not pink/red (ruling out Gibberella/Fusarium), not white (ruling out Diplodia)

The first Trichoderma reference (Corn_Disease_26.jpg) was the closest visual match to the test image among all references viewed.
